chapter: Pay, the Fletcher Henderson circle and later life
title: Fletcher's Roseland band, Joe Smith and Howard Scott
summary: He lists men in Fletcher Henderson's Roseland band and admires Joe Smith's muted style, shared only by Howard Scott.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: That's true. They were the first call him Smack colored band in the Roseland Ballroom, and we'd go and inspect for (unintelligible) short -- that was the nickname. And Smack got all them fellows, Buster and Don Redmon, Coleman Hawkins, Joe Smith. You know, Joe had three brothers. See, there's about seven of them brothers. But there's a brother -- a lot of them have worked with Fletcher one time, Pops -- Russell MR. : (Unintelligible). MR. CALDWELL: Yeah. But you know who was the best
Yeah. But I mean don't you think Joe Smith was an absolutely exceptional trumpet?
He was. Nobody had ever -- there was one fellow that had Joe's style with a mute. He had a beautiful style. It was Howard Scott-- worked with Fletcher.
And Howard Scott is still alive.
Still alive. We all along belong to the same musician club.
